Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The unemployment rate is 8.8% and falling (down 0.6 over 3 months), with fed funds at 0.09%, so this looks like early 2011. Headline CPI is 2.7% YoY, which fits February 2011 (it was 2.1% in February and 2.7% in March 2011). Core CPI at 1.19% matches roughly early 2011. The 10-year yield at 3.34% fits March 2011 (about 3.4%).

Unemployment was 8.8% in March 2011, and 8.9% in February. Payrolls averaged about 159k over three months, which also fits March 2011.

Gold rose 9.9% in the month, which doesn't fit March 2011, when gold was roughly +1%. Gold gained about 32% over 12 months, consistent with early 2011. A 1-month gain of 9.9% fits better with the period from Aug to Dec 2010. VIX at 14.62 is low, which suggests a month like December 2010 or February 2011, but December 2010 had unemployment at 9.4%, so it doesn't fit.

Equity gains of +2.8% over 1 month and 17% over 12 months, with developed ex-US +5.1%, fit March 2011 less well, because the Japan earthquake pulled markets down that month. April 2011 fits better: unemployment was 9.0% then, and the VIX was around 14.6. Gold rose about 7.6% in April, and ex-US equities rose about 5%. Headline CPI was 3.2% in April.

Unemployment at 8.8% was reported for March 2011 and the CPI figure was 2.7%, so the data seem to be a March reading. But the market numbers look like April, with the 10-year yield at 3.34% and 7-10y Treasuries up 1.6% in the month. Mixed signals, so I'll settle on April 2011 with the 3-month unemployment change of -0.6 (9.4 to 8.8), which is consistent with a reference date of March or April.
